item.title: 40th memorial: Media icons pay tributes to ‘Dele Giwa’s Granite Journalism’
item.description: •Giwa had premonition of his death — Osoba By Sebastine Obasi Media icons yesterday converged on the Nigerian Institute of Journalism, NIJ, Ogba, Lagos, where they paid tributes to Dele Giwa, one of Nigeria’s journalism icons. The occasion was the book presentation to mark the 40th anniversary of the death of Dele Giwa, Co-founder of Newswatch magazine, who was assassinated through a parcel bomb on October 19, 1986. The event drew media icons and eminent Nigerians such as former governor, Segun Osoba, Nduka Obaigbena, publisher, ThisDay, Newspapers, Yemi Ogunbiyi, former managing director, Daily Times, Biodun Shobanjo, former Chaiman, Insight Communications, Ralp Akinfeleye, emeritus professor, University of Lagos, Nosa Igiebor, Co-founder, Tell Magazine, Chuka Momah, ace columnist, Gbenga Adefaye, Provost, Nigerian Institute of Journalism, Funmi and Aisha, Dele Giwa’s wife and daughter, respectively. Founder and Publisher of Vanguard Newspapers, Sam Amuka, who was the Chairman of the occasion, described late Dele Giwa, Co-founder, Newswatch magazine, as a true legend and patriotic Nigerian journalist during his lifetime. Amuka stated this at the book presentation on Dele Giwa’s Granite Journalism, held at the Kesington Adebutu Auditorium, NIJ, Ogba, Lagos. Amuka, who recalled Giwa’s popular saying, ‘’protest pays” also stated that it takes a legend to propound such theory, which has proven to be right, especially in the Nigerian context. For him, though Giwa died at 39, his legacy lives. He enjoined the audience, as well as other Nigerians to buy the book, which he said, it worth reading. Also, speaking, Ray Ekpu, Co-founder of Newswatch magazine, stated that Giwa was a blessing to Nigeria’s journalism, as he brought to bear, his high intellect and engaging investigation into the profession. Ekpu described Giwa’s untimely death by a parcel bomb, as deeply devastating to the Newswatch family, who made humanly efforts to unravel the killers without success. Going down memory lane, former governor, Segun Osoba, who was managing director of Times, stated how a day before his death, Giwa had complained to his colleagues at an event at Victoria Island that security personnel were after his life. An urgent meeting was arranged between the journalists and Augustus Aikhomu, then Chief of General Staff, who assured them that he would investigate the matter. Osoba commended Giwa’s courage and sense of patriotism. For Yemi Ogunbiyi, former managing director of Daily Times, Giwa was a remarkable human being, who added colour and vibrancy to Nigeria’s journalism. For Biodun Shobanjo, public relations czar, Dele Giwa was an enigma, as he was larger than life. “We should all take pride in having Giwa as a husband, colleague, riend and fantastic journalistic,” he added. Aisha DeleGiwa’s daughter, stated that though he was one year old, when the father died, the stories told about him by her mother and all what she has read made her believe that Giwa died a marty

item.title: With subsidy, Naira’ll exchange at N4,000/$ — Oyedele
item.description: *I’ve no regret on subsidy removal, we can’t go back to Egypt — Tinubu *ADC takes on Oyedele over N4,000/$ claim *Ask him to provide evidence, stop using fear to discourage debate *Economy would have collapsed without Tinubu’s reforms, says Shettima *Assures food prices’ll come down soon By Clifford Ndujihe, Johnbosco Agbakwuru & Luminous Jannamike LAGOS — The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has warned Nigerians against returning to petrol subsidy. Read Also: Subsidy removal: I’ve no regret, we can’t go back to Egypt — Tinubu Oyedele said the return could trigger capital flight, undermine investor confidence and push the naira to N3,000, N3,500, or even N4,000 per dollar. He disclosed this at a press briefing of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, yesterday. In a quick counter, the Presidential Campaign Council, PCC, of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, challenged the minister to produce models showing that giving Nigerians fuel subsidy will hurt the Naira, adding that the Federal Government is discouraging debate on fuel subsidy removal through fear mongering. ADC presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, has promised a return to fuel subsidy if elected, to cushion the hardship faced by the citizenry. Oyedele’s argument The minister said investors had repeatedly questioned whether government would abandon its reforms ahead of the next election cycle. Oyedele, who ruled out reversing the government’s economic reforms, maintained that any signal that President Bola Tinubu’s administration is contemplating reinstating subsidy will immediately affect financial markets, raise borrowing costs and worsen economic pressures on households. “In all the meetings I have had, I came to a conclusion that the markets, including the domestic market, which you can read from the capital market, and the international market, have largely written off the opposition in Nigeria as being unserious. “If, for any reason, the President were to say we are merely considering the return of fuel subsidy, capital would react immediately. Air fares would struggle, the naira would come under severe pressure, potentially moving towards N3,000, N3,500 or even N4,000. The very fuel people want subsidised would become far more expensive in naira terms,” he said. Oyedele warned that capital flight could extend beyond foreign investors, as wealthy Nigerians, business owners and middle-class investors might also seek refuge in dollars, further increasing demand for foreign exchange. He stressed that ordinary Nigerians will ultimately bear the consequences through higher import costs, rising prices and increased economic hardship. The minister also rejected the description of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited’s temporary reduction in petrol retail margins as a return to subsidy, explaining that it is a commercial decision rather than a payment funded by public resources.

In the recent changes at INEC, Mrs Oluyemi Titilayo Adeyemi-Showunmi, formerly the Administrative Secretary of the commission’s Lagos State office, was redeployed as the Director of Electoral Operations at the commission. She is the wife of Segun Showunmi, a spokesman for the Tinubu/Shettima 2027 Presidential Campaign Council. Prof. Mustapha Aliu, identified as an elder brother of Sokoto State Governor, Ahmed Aliyu, who is seeking a second term on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), has also been nominated as an INEC commissioner. According to reports, Isah Magaji Gummi, who previously headed the Electoral Operations Department, was redeployed to the Voter Registry Department. The Electoral Operations Department plays a key role in election planning and implementation, including the coordination of polling arrangements, deployment of election materials and management of personnel involved in electoral operations. Although the director of the department does not independently determine election results, the responsibilities attached to the office have drawn attention to the redeployment and calls for INEC to explain the considerations behind the decision. Adeyemi-Showunmi’s redeployment has sparked debate among civil society organisations and on social media over transparency, political neutrality and public confidence in the electoral body. Former director of voter education at INEC, Mr Nick Dazang, when contacted said, it would be wrong for the Commission to pretend that appointing someone that close to a sitting governor who is contesting elections has no implications. “The person may be eminently qualified but I have profound misgivings if he can discharge or execute his office as Resident Electoral Commissioner with the professionalism, neutrality and impartiality that the office demands. On the redeployment of Sowunmi wife, he said in the time past, and oblivious of the closeness/proximity of INEC officials to certain politically exposed persons, INEC officials on their merit, had been inadvertently assigned to roles/tasks that put them in difficult positions which complicated the Commission’s core values of impartiality and neutrality. He said In such circumstances, and in deference to its core values, INEC has demonstrated sensitivity by not posting such deserving officials to these positions. “It is likely that the Commission may not be aware or cognizant of the said officer’s relationship with a prominent politician. “But once this is established, and its attention is called to this reality, it should promptly do the needful, namely: not to put the officer in a position that compromises the Commission’s principles of neutrality and provision of a level playing field to all contestants. In the prevailing circumstance, the officer should be directed to recuse herself. This will allay fears, rightly or wrongly, that she has been procured to deliberately confer an advantage to any candidate(s) in the election. Either the tenure of the subsisting Director is specially extended for the period of the election, or his Deputy is directed to act in the position of Director, subject to consideration(s) of merit, federal character and the core values aforementioned,” he added. Director-General of YIAGA Africa, Samson Itodo, warned that the electoral body must ensure public confidence in the electoral process and should not take the people for granted in its appointment. On the appointment of Adeyemi-Showunmi as INEC Director of Electoral Operations, Itodo said elections are fundamentally about operations, adding that by this token, it is one of the most sensitive and consequential departments within INEC. He said, “In fact, the Electoral Operations Department is at the heart of election administration. From the recruitment and deployment of polling officials to the planning, production and distribution of election materials, as well as the operational arrangements for voting and results collation, the department plays a central role in determining how elections are conducted. “Mrs. Showunmi’s competence and professional capacity are not in doubt. However, competence alone is not sufficient for appointments to sensitive positions in election management. The independence, impartiality and perceived neutrality of those entrusted with managing elections are equally important. “Appointing individuals with strong ties to politicians in such strategic positions inevitably raises legitimate questions about impartiality and INEC independence. These concerns become even more pronounced in a climate of deep public distrust, growing fears of political capture of INEC, and politicians boldly declaring the number of votes they expect to secure before a single ballot has been cast. “At a time when public confidence in the electoral process is already fragile, appointments to critical positions within INEC should inspire confidence, not deepen suspicion. INEC must recognize that its credibility rests not only on the technical competence of its personnel but also on public confidence in INEC’s independence from partisan interests. Public confidence in the electoral process must never be taken for granted. In this instance, it is being taken for granted,” he said. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar was among those who first raised the alarm over the issue, demanding immediate and full transparency from INEC. In a statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said the reported changes in the Electoral Operations Department raised serious questions that INEC must answer without delay. “Reports indicate that Director Isa Magaji Gummi was moved from Electoral Operations to the Voter Registry Department, while Mrs Oluyemi Titilayo Adeyemi-Showunmi was appointed to head Electoral Operations. Dr Lawrence Bayode has also been identified as the head of Information and Communication Technology (ICT). “These departments are at the heart of election administration. INEC must explain these decisions, publish the criteria applied and show that every appointment and redeployment followed due process, was based on merit and was free from political interference. Nigerians will not accept vague assurances on matters this serious.” Atiku said no official should be presumed compromised because of their ethnicity, background or associations. But when reported political connections or a concentration of appointments raises public concern, INEC must provide verifiable assurances that its impartiality is protected. “A government that has driven millions of Nigerians into hardship must not be allowed to turn the electoral umpire into an instrument of political survival. When sensitive election departments are reshaped and major contracts are surrounded by unanswered questions, the suspicion that a failing administration is seeking every possible advantage to cling to power will only grow. INEC must dispel that suspicion through full, immediate and verifiable disclosure,” he said. A political analyst, Professor Saleh Dauda, maintained that political undertones cannot be ruled out in the redeployment of Adeyemi-Showunmi ahead of the general elections. He added that Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, had promised support for the initiative in the state. He urged the Federal Government to collaborate with the affected state governments to remove administrative and other obstacles delaying the establishment and operation of the centres. According to him, effective implementation of the guidelines, alongside stronger penalties, would help strengthen the medicine supply chain and improve patient safety. The PSN president also warned against placing the responsibility for identifying fake medicines on patients, insisting that pharmacists and other qualified professionals had a critical role to play in protecting consumers. He said manufacturers conducted quality-control checks before releasing medicines to the market, while some companies had introduced product-verification systems to help detect suspected counterfeits. “It is not the job of a patient to check or confirm whether a drug is fake or not. On the rising cost of medicines, the PSN president said government incentives for pharmaceutical manufacturers would have limited impact unless authorities addressed the broader costs of local production. He explained that reductions in import tariffs alone might not translate into cheaper medicines if manufacturers continued to face high diesel prices, electricity costs and transportation expenses. “Unless the government takes a holistic view of the drivers of the prices of pharmaceuticals, we are not going to see any appreciable decrease in the cost of drugs,” he said. He also called for stronger collaboration between government agencies responsible for natural-product research and pharmaceutical manufacturers to develop promising research findings into medicines for local use. The PSN president warned that the high cost of medicines was pushing some Nigerians away from conventional healthcare towards traditional remedies, underscoring the need to improve access to affordable and quality-assured medicines. Meanwhile, PSN National Secretary, Pharm. Gafar Madehein, cautioned Nigerians against assuming that herbal products were safe simply because they carried NAFDAC registration numbers. He explained that a registration number issued for listing purposes did not necessarily mean that a product had undergone clinical trials demonstrating its safety and efficacy. Madehein also warned that combining herbal remedies with conventional medicines could trigger harmful interactions, urging consumers to seek professional advice before using them together. item.title: Catholic bishops declare nationwide fasting, prayer
item.description: The Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria, CBCN, has declared a nationwide prayer and fasting programme to promote free, fair, credible and peaceful elections in 2027. The programme, themed ‘Let Justice and Peace Flow’, is drawn from Amos 5:24. The bishops announced the initiative in a statement signed by their President, Archbishop Matthew Ndagoso, and Secretary, Bishop Peter Odetoyinbo, yesterday in Abuja. They said the programme was necessary as Nigeria approached the 2027 general elections amid recurring challenges of electoral violence, rigging, vote-buying and ethno-religious divisions. The bishops urged dioceses, parishes, church societies, prayer groups, families and individuals to participate actively in the spiritual exercise. They said the initiative was aimed at seeking God’s guidance for electoral officials and security personnel to discharge their responsibilities faithfully, while inspiring citizens to vote conscientiously and discouraging electoral malpractice and violence. According to the statement, all parishes would observe October 31 and November 28 as days of prayer and fasting for Nigeria. Activities would include fasting, the Rosary procession, Holy Mass and the recitation of the CBCN prayer for the 2027 elections. The bishops also designated December 8, the Solemnity of the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary, as a nationwide diocesan day of prayer. The programme would begin with Holy Mass at 3 p.m., presided over by the diocesan bishop, during which a pastoral letter titled “2027 Elections: Call to Responsible Choice and Action” would be read. The Mass would be followed by a Rosary procession to the cathedral at 4:30 p.m. and conclude with Eucharistic Benediction. The statement further declared January 15, 2027, the eve of the general elections, a nationwide parish day of prayer and fasting. The bishops urged Nigerians to reject tribalism, corruption, bribery and voter apathy, while encouraging citizens to vote and protect their votes peacefully. They called for a credible electoral process free from rancour and bloodshed. The post Catholic bishops declare nationwide fasting, prayer appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Doctors top global trust rankings as politicians, influencers come last
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe Medical doctors, scientists and teachers are the most trusted professions globally, while politicians and social media influencers rank among the least trusted, according to a survey of 23,530 online adults under 75 across 32 countries. The survey, known as the Ipsos Global Trustworthiness Index 2026, conducted by Ipsos, an international market research and public opinion polling company, showed that doctors lead the rankings, with 58 percent of respondents expressing trust in them, followed by scientists at 56 percent and teachers at 54 percent. Restaurant serving staff ranked fourth at 44 percent, followed by the armed forces at 43 percent. Police officers, judges and ordinary men and women each recorded 38 percent, while lawyers received 31 percent. Television news anchors recorded 30 percent, while pollsters and clergy or priests each scored 29 percent. Taxi drivers and civil servants followed at 28 percent. Journalists and bankers each recorded 27 percent, while business leaders scored 26 percent. At the lower end, government ministers recorded 20 per cent, followed by advertising executives at 19 per cent. Social media influencers and politicians generally ranked last, with 15 per cent each. The percentages represent the share of respondents expressing trust in each profession or group, not those selecting it as their single most trusted occupation. The precise survey question and response options should be verified against the original Ipsos report. The findings highlight a marked contrast between trust in health and scientific professionals and confidence in political figures and social surveys. All the defendants had pleaded not guilty, repeatedly maintaining that nobody had been forced to die. The pastor usually began preaching at noon, with some sessions featuring what was described as “casting out demons”. After the church’s main branch shut down in 2019, Mackenzie relocated to Shakahola forest and encouraged his followers to move there. Among those who followed him was Peter Shukrani, 23, who relocated to the forest with his mother. He had joined the church at the age of eight and considered Mackenzie his “spiritual father”. Despite his experiences, Shukrani said he would “never say a bad word about him”. However, he fell ill while living in the forest, where medication was prohibited. His condition worsened after his mother discarded the medicines he needed. “My mother would throw away all the medicine I was supposed to take because she believe that only God could heal me,” Shukrani said. Karisa said some victims were so severely weakened by starvation that they died while being transported out of the forest. “We would carry someone out of the forest but they were so frail that they would die in our arms,” he said. Despite accounts of starvation, strangulation and bludgeoning among the victims, Shukrani continued to defend Mackenzie before the verdict. He described the pastor as “a good person who cares for me”. “Mackenzie didn’t force anyone to fast. People made those choices by themselves because of their beliefs. I still love him and he is still my pastor,” Shukrani said. Dan Mackenzie, however, argued before the ruling that his father should be held responsible for the deaths because of his leadership position within the group. “He was the leader, he was someone who they were looking [up to]. item.title: Customs to review complaints of 397 rejected recruitment applicants
item.description: By Efe Onodjae The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has announced plans to review complaints by applicants who were disqualified during its recent recruitment screening exercise despite appearing on the shortlist for training. The Service said the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, ordered a case-by-case review after meeting with some of the aggrieved applicants. In a statement signed by the National Public Relations Officer of the NCS, Deputy Comptroller of Customs Abdullahi Maiwada, on Monday, the NCS said the review was aimed at ensuring that legitimate complaints were examined while maintaining the integrity of the recruitment process. It explained that appearing on the final shortlist did not automatically guarantee enlistment, as applicants were required to undergo several stages of verification, including credential checks, physical fitness assessments, medical examinations, age verification and drug screening. According to the Service, screening irregularities involving 397 applicants were identified in areas including substance use, physical fitness, medical records, age and submitted documentation. It added that some candidates were also disqualified over irregularities identified in their selection process. The NCS urged affected applicants who believe they were unfairly disqualified to submit their details and complaints to helpdesk@customs.gov.ng for review. It said applicants seeking reconsideration would be subjected to fresh screening, stressing that the review would not automatically guarantee admission into the training college. The Service further warned that applicants found to have engaged in criminal conduct, including certificate fraud and other offences, would be referred for appropriate legal action and prosecution. It urged the affected candidates and the general public to remain calm and use the designated channel to submit their complaints. item.title: ‘Close up your borders’ – Trump blames French unrest on immigration
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Monday again blamed immigration for protests and violence that have rocked France in recent days, urging Europe and French President Emmanuel Macron to tighten borders. “What’s happening in France has to do with immigration, not schools, not anything,” Trump told reporters in Washington, echoing his comments from the day before. “It’s immigration, and I told President Emmanuel Macron, close up your borders.” Weekend demonstrations over soaring prices were held in Paris and other cities, degenerating into some of the worst street violence France has seen in recent years. Trump recounted a conversation with Macron, telling him “a long time ago, you’re making a big mistake in France. You’re letting everybody from the world come in. The whole world was coming in. “Paris is going to be a Muslim city very soon,” the 80-year-old Republican added. “If Europe doesn’t close its borders and bring the criminals out, like the people that are protesting, Europe is finished.” Trump made combating illegal immigration a central pledge of his 2024 campaign, at times relying on false claims that played on racial fears. item.title: Maddison shines as Tottenham claim long-awaited first PL win of season
item.description: James Maddison made a sensational return to Tottenham’s starting line-up after 17 months away on Monday as Spurs beat Coventry 3-1 to claim their long-awaited first Premier League win of the season. The England midfielder has featured only fleetingly since May 2025, when he suffered the first of two serious knee injuries. But Maddison needed less than a quarter of an hour to put Spurs ahead at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium with a stunning first-time strike from outside the penalty area. Jack Rudoni levelled early in the second half but the home side were back in front just before the hour mark when Omar Marmoush lashed home his first goal for the club and substitute Ben Davies made the points safe late on. Roberto De Zerbi’s team came into the match bottom of the Premier League and with the unwanted record of being the only team in England’s top six divisions without a league win this season despite a huge summer spend. The Spurs boss had taken his squad to Marbella in southern Spain for some warm-weather training in a bid to kickstart their season. He named Maddison in his starting line-up while Sweden midfielder Dejan Kulusevski returned to the matchday squad for the first time in 17 months. Maddison ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in August 2025, just three months after injuring the same knee. The 29-year-old wasted little time in making his mark, putting his side ahead in the 14th minute in spectacular style after fine work from Mohammed Kudus on the right. Maddison, lurking just outside the penalty area, received the ball from Kudus and sent it curling past Coventry goalkeeper Carl Rushworth and into the top corner, sparking wild scenes of delight among the home fans. Tottenham now had their tails up and threatened to overwhelm the visitors but Frank Lampard’s newly promoted Coventry, who had won their previous two games, re-established a foothold. Maddison went close to putting Spurs 2-0 after half an hour but his half-cross, half-shot curled narrowly wide. But they failed to stretch their lead and Coventry were level in the 49th minute, courtesy of a Rudoni strike from close range. Spurs lost the ball in the Coventry half and the visitors swept forward. Rudoni’s cross hit a teammate but the ball fell kindly for him and he drove home. Just nine minutes later Spurs were back in front when former Manchester City forward Marmoush held off Milan van Ewijk before unleashing an unstoppable shot. Kulusevski, who suffered a knee injury in May 2025, was introduced in the final minutes to a huge ovation from the home fans. Spurs veteran Davies made the three points safe deep into added time, poking home from the edge of the penalty area as Tottenham could at last relax. item.title: Drone Strikes Across Sudan Kill More Than 100 People
item.description: A wave of drone strikes targeting war-torn Sudan’s army-held capital Khartoum and two western areas controlled by paramilitary forces has killed more than 100 people since Sunday, according to residents, medical workers and paramilitary sources. The deadliest drone strike hit near a market on Sunday evening in Al-Dibab town in the southwestern state of West Kordofan, which is controlled by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) that have been at war with Sudan’s military since April 2023. Residents and medical workers said a drone struck a transport hub where villagers had gathered after a market day to find rides home, killing 80 people. Ahmed Abakar Wadi, a resident who helped bury victims, told AFP at least 50 bodies were recovered at the scene, including that of his brother. Another 47 wounded people were taken to the nearby town of Al-Mujlad where 30 later died from their injuries, according to a medical source. “The drone struck once, and then came back 10 minutes later and struck again,” Wadi told AFP. The RSF’s self-declared administration, known as Tasis, and the Sudanese rights group Emergency Lawyers accused the army of carrying out the attack. The military has not commented. The strike was one of the deadliest single attacks in Kordofan, an oil-rich region linking western and eastern Sudan where the army and the RSF have been battling for territory. item.title: ‘You Cannot Ask Moses To Go Back To Egypt,’ Tinubu Insists No Fuel Subsidy Return
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has reiterated that there will be no return to the fuel subsidy regime, insisting that his administration took a bold and necessary step to reform the country’s economy. Tinubu spoke on Monday during a meeting with the City Boy Movement, a youth-driven political and advocacy group founded to champion his administration’s agenda. “I came, and I removed the subsidy on my first day. Nigeria would have gone bankrupt; there was nothing left to pay for subsidies,” he said. “I could listen to my political opponents promising a return to subsidy.” Drawing a religious analogy, the president added, “I remember my scripture studies, both in the Bible and the Holy Quran. When Moses (Musa) left Egypt, the Red Sea parted and gave way. You cannot ask Moses to go back to Egypt. With your energy and support, we will never go back to Egypt.” The former Lagos State governor commended the organisation for drumming up support for his administration and urged members to take his government’s achievements to the grassroots. “Those of you who are lucky to work with me have given me all the answers needed and the confidence required to see the coming election as a simple matter,” Tinubu stated. “You will go to your campuses, your markets, and your villages. Make sure every young person you know has a PVC and uses it. Tell them what we have done and tell them what we will do. Campaign with your ideas.” President Tinubu announced an end to fuel subsidy during his inauguration in May 2023. The policy shift sparked an immediate hike in petrol pump prices, rising from under ₦200 per litre to current rates hovering between ₦1,350 and ₦1,405 per litre across major filling stations. While the policy has drawn widespread criticism over the heightened cost of living, the president remains firm on his stance. The federal government maintains that the decision is essential to reset the national economy, reassuring citizens that the initial economic hardship will ease over time.
